commit_message:
Route git linked-worktree files to the correct window (#290708, #299540)

findWindowOnFile matched windows by simple parent-folder containment of
a file's path. Git linked worktrees store their private per-worktree
files (COMMIT_EDITMSG, rebase-merge/git-rebase-todo, etc.) inside the
*main* worktree's .git/worktrees/<name> directory rather than under the
linked worktree's own folder, so such files always resolved to the main
worktree's window instead of the correct linked-worktree window (e.g.
when core.editor is "code --wait").

Add findWindowOnGitWorktreeFile, checked before the existing
parent-folder matching: it recognizes .git/worktrees/<name> metadata
paths and, by resolving each candidate window's own .git pointer file,
matches against the full worktree directory path rather than just the
trailing <name> segment, so two unrelated repositories that happen to
share a worktree name cannot be confused with one another. Ordinary
repositories (.git as a directory) and non-worktree files are
unaffected and never trigger the new filesystem read.

commit_message:
Fix forked process console forwarding reporting shared references as circular

The JSON.stringify replacer in bootstrap-fork's safeToString pushed every
object into a `seen` array and never removed anything, so a value that is
referenced twice in the console arguments of a forked process (a DAG, not
a cycle) was forwarded to the parent as "[Circular]" after its first
occurrence. For example console.log(shared, { a: shared, b: shared })
arrived as [{"value":1},{"a":"[Circular]","b":"[Circular]"}].

Track only the current ancestor path instead, using the replacer's `this`
(the holder) to drop subtrees that are finished. True cycles are still
reported as "[Circular]". The isObject helper is gone: every object has
to be tracked for the holder check to work, and RegExp/Date were the only
exclusions (a Date is already a string by the time the replacer sees it).

Added an integration test that forks bootstrap-fork with a fixture that
logs a shared reference and a genuine cycle.

commit_message:
Fix safeStringify treating shared references as circular

safeStringify kept every object it had seen in a Set and never removed
anything, so a value that appears in two sibling branches (a DAG, not a
cycle) was replaced with "[Circular]" on every occurrence after the
first. For example safeStringify([shared, { x: shared }]) returned
[{"a":1},{"x":"[Circular]"}].

Track only the current ancestor path instead, using the replacer's
`this` (the holder) to drop subtrees that are finished. True cycles are
still reported as "[Circular]". This is the same change that was made
to stableStringify in #327398.

The existing safeStringify test encoded the old behaviour: obj2 is both
obj1.friend and a sibling in `c`, so its second occurrence is shared,
not circular. Updated that expectation and added a test for shared
references in object and array positions.

commit_message:
Preserve collapse state in the SCM Repositories view

The Repositories view re-expanded a repository that has submodules every
time the view became visible, so a collapsed parent repository could not
be kept collapsed.

Two things caused this:

- The tree input was always set with the view state that was read from
  storage once in `renderBody`. That state is only written on
  `onWillSaveState`, so any expand/collapse done in the meantime was
  discarded when the view became visible again. Capture the current view
  state when the view is hidden and use it on the next show instead.
- When the view became visible, all known repositories were re-registered
  through `onDidAddRepository`, and for a repository with a `parentId`
  that unconditionally expanded the parent. Only expand the parent when it
  actually gains its first child repository.

commit_message:
Fix "Upstream already exists" when creating a fork

The GitHub push error handler hardcoded the `upstream` and `origin` remote
names when creating a fork after a permission denied push. When the
repository already had a remote using one of those names - which is the
common case when forking a fork - `git remote rename` failed with
"remote upstream already exists" and the whole fork flow was aborted.

Fall back to a suffixed name (`upstream-1`, `origin-1`, ...) when the
preferred name is already taken. Repositories without such remotes keep
using `upstream`/`origin` exactly as before.

Fixes #160377

commit_message:
Give WorkbenchButtonBar ownership of icon-label spacing

WorkbenchButtonBar now owns the relationship between a leading
icon/spinner and its label instead of splitting it across a child
margin and, in some consumers, a parent gap:

- The leading slot is sized from --vscode-iconSize-small (16px) and
  carries zero margin of its own.
- The button expresses the relationship as column-gap, defaulting to
  the existing 4px appearance. An opt-in iconLabelSpacing: 'default'
  variant uses 6px for buttons that want an existing wider visual
  relationship.
- The Changes view's primary labelled button migrates from a
  distributed 2px container gap + 4px child margin (effectively 6px)
  to a single 6px control-owned gap via iconLabelSpacing: 'default',
  preserving its current appearance. Its diff-stat line counts keep
  their own 2px gap, which was never part of this relationship.

This is the first shared-control pilot for the predictable UI
composition proposal, stacked on the authoring guidance in
cherwan/ui-composition-authoring-guidance.

commit_message:
Fix flaky sub-pixel margin comparison in inline-icon test

CI's macOS / Browser lane has been failing this test across several
recent commits with a sub-pixel mismatch (3.2px vs 3.1875px) between
the inline icon's computed marginInlineStart and marginInlineEnd. Both
values come from the same symmetric, font-metric-derived margin, and
differ only by rendering-engine rounding, not by an actual asymmetry.
Compare them numerically with a small tolerance instead of exact
string equality so the test asserts symmetry without depending on
sub-pixel rounding matching bit-for-bit across platforms.

while the existing tie-break (<=) still rounds an exact 0.5px tie up
to 1px as documented.

commit_message:
Terminal: tolerate float error when scaling charHeight to device pixels

getXtermScaledDimensions ceils charHeight * devicePixelRatio, but charHeight
comes from xterm's device cell height divided by devicePixelRatio, so the
product can land a few ulps above the whole pixel. At zoom level 1 a 22 px
cell becomes 23 px in the row math, dropping one row per ~20 and leaving
blank rows above the grid.

commit_message:
sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization

The V3 new-session onboarding personalizes its 3 prompt options with GitHub
items, falling back to standard options. Telemetry from experiment f716301b
showed 61% of impressions timed out with zero GitHub options, and the existing
events could not measure partial success: `fallbackReason` was only 'none' when
all 3 slots were GitHub, so 2 real issues logged identically to zero.

Telemetry (additive; existing field names and values unchanged):
- promptStrategy gains gitHubOptionCount, candidatesFound, lookupDurationMs,
  per-stage durations and outcomes, and timedOutStage.
- promptOptionInteraction gains optionIndex and optionKindsShown, so per-option
  CTR is computable rather than confounded with availability.
- Both gain a shared impressionId, replacing lossy DevDeviceId joins.
- New 'noComposer' fallback reason splits the infra-bug meaning out of the
  overloaded 'noCandidate'.
- Bounded categories and counts only: no titles, URLs, numbers, repository
  names or prompt text.

Latency, without raising the 10s total budget:
- Publish issue candidates before the linkage lookup, which only filters out
  issues that already have linked pull requests and so must never hide them.
- Keep review-thread enrichment off the critical path; it produced the least
  picked option while being the most expensive stage.
- Rebalance sub-budgets to 4000/1500/3000 so the concurrent chains fit.
- Stream options into the composer: paint the standard options immediately and
  replace slots as lookups land, instead of blocking first paint on the lookup.

INewSessionPromptOptionsController.resolve gains an optional progress callback
that reports whether an update was rendered, so the composer can refuse late
updates while the user is acting on the options and telemetry still describes
what was actually shown.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
remote: fix managed resource loading from workbench

Chromium omits referrers for requests originating from the vscode-file
scheme because custom schemes are not registered as allowed referrer
sources. The protocol level referrer check therefore rejected every
legitimate managed remote resource request from the workbench.

Remove the unreliable referrer check and rely on the existing
webRequest frame tree validation, which rejects requests originating
from vscode-webview frames using browser owned frame identity.

Also return Buffer instances for error responses from the buffer
protocol handler. String response bodies are invalid for
registerBufferProtocol and caused intended HTTP error responses to
surface as net::ERR_FAILED.

commit_message:
Acquire a process lock on the session data directory

The main IPC handle is scoped to the product version, so right after an
update the new process fails to detect the old one via claimInstance and
both processes end up using the same user data directory at the same
time. Chromium does not support sharing session data between multiple
running browser processes and webview service worker registration then
fails with an InvalidStateError.

Add a version independent process lock for the session data:

- createStaticIPCHandle now allows omitting the version so that the same
  handle is produced by all versions for a given user data directory
  (existing callers are unchanged)
- the main process serves that handle (environmentMainService.
  sessionDataLockHandle) for its whole lifetime before any storage in the
  user data directory is opened (claimSessionData runs right after
  claimInstance and before initServices)
- if a live lock holder exists, the process waits for it to exit (polling
  every second, dialog after 10s with Keep Waiting/Exit that re-appears
  every 60s), because concurrent use of the session data directory is
  unsupported and can corrupt Chromium state storage
- stale sockets of dead processes are recovered by probing the handle and
  unlinking it, mirroring claimInstance; the lock is released on shutdown

Signed-off-by: Danila Fominykh <d@m8sh.su>
author: dnch13

commit_message:
Treat ENOENT when probing the session data lock as a released lock

A normal lock release can remove the Unix socket in between the failed
serve() attempt and the connect() probe (and on Windows the named pipe
disappears when its owning process exits). The probe then failed with
ENOENT, which escaped and aborted startup instead of continuing the
polling loop. Treat ENOENT as a released-lock race and retry
acquisition.

The same race applies to the unlink() of a stale socket, which another
process may have removed in the meantime: ignore ENOENT there quietly
instead of logging a warning.

Signed-off-by: Danila Fominykh <d@m8sh.su>

commit_message:
diffEditor: Center the gutter between both editors

The gutter that holds the hunk actions was carved out of the original
editor alone, so the two sides of a side-by-side diff were never the
same width. Both editors now give up half of it.

The edges of the gap are snapped to whole pixels rather than split at
`sashLeft +/- gutterWidth / 2`, so each editor always gets an integer
width and the gap absorbs the leftover pixel. A fractional width would
be floored by `EditorLayoutInfoComputer.computeLayout` and painted at
that size anyway, so it would not keep the editors flush, would wrap one
side a column earlier than the other, and would move the border of the
modified editor off the pixel grid.

`SashLayout.getGutterEdges` is the single definition of that geometry;
the layout and both sashes read it, which keeps the drag handles on the
edges of the gap instead of half a pixel beside them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
author: M393

commit_message:
diffEditor: Keep the minimum editor width on both sides of the gutter

`sashLeft` is clamped so that `MINIMUM_EDITOR_WIDTH` remains beside the
split point, which held while the gutter hung off one side of it. Now
that the gutter straddles the split point, each editor starts half a
gutter further in, leaving both sides 82px instead of 100px at the
limits of a drag.

Clamp in `getGutterEdges` instead, where the gutter width is known, so
the minimum applies to the edges the editors actually get. This also
covers the original editor, which used to drop to 65px at the left limit
because the gutter was taken from that side alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: only remove worktree on archive when in sync with remote

Previously worktree cleanup on archive committed any local changes and then
removed the worktree, relying on branch preservation for safety. Instead,
gate removal on the branch being fully up to date with its remote: it must
track an upstream branch, have no unpushed commits, and have a clean working
tree. The check fails closed when git state can't be determined, so no
local-only work is ever discarded.

commit_message:
fix: center the fork glyph in the chat checkpoint toolbar

The checkpoint toolbar renders the fork icon at the compact 12px size,
but the generic actionbar rule gives any descendant codicon a 16px flex
box with no horizontal alignment. The 12px glyph was left-aligned inside
that box, leaving the unused 4px on its right and shifting the icon ~2px
off-center inside an otherwise symmetric button.

Center the glyph within its icon box. Button size, padding, divider
lines, and Restore Checkpoint placement are unchanged, and the compact
loading spinner that reuses the same span is centered too.

Both the chat view and the Agents Window render this control through the
shared ChatForkActionViewItem, so a single scoped rule fixes both.
